scope: Only selected current Sync R2, RML and remote workflow clauses/actions; no repository-wide absence claim. Frozen snapshots substitute for mutable current wiki pins; current canonicals were consulted and matched these snapshot bytes.

references.quoted_scoped_predicate: MIDI Clock provides tempo-dependent ticks and song-position messages. Changing the sync host tempo is described as causing the receiving device to follow the change; Live can act as sender/sync host or receiver/device. No byte encoding, tick count, filtering, MIDI transport command sequence, numerical tracking/convergence or timestamp law is established.
references.assessment: context/partial prerequisite only; does not specify named Hardware Resync selector, button action or its three mode roles

references.quoted_scoped_predicate: Enable the connected sequencer as a sync destination in Tempo & MIDI Settings and configure it to receive MIDI sync. The lower LED beside EXT flashes while Live sends sync messages. Indicator activity alone proves neither receiving-device synchronization nor usable signal timing.
references.assessment: context/partial prerequisite only; does not specify named Hardware Resync selector, button action or its three mode roles

references.quoted_scoped_predicate: Selecting a MIDI device exposes its Sync Delay control, which delays Live's internal time base relative to the sync signal. The chapter suggests aligning separately audible percussive patterns by listening. No range, sign law, sample precision, jitter tolerance or calibration result is supplied.
references.assessment: context/partial prerequisite only; does not specify named Hardware Resync selector, button action or its three mode roles

references.quoted_scoped_predicate: Use independently admitted compatible MIDI receiver/transmitter and retain genuine usable source traffic before separately configuring Live Clock-host and Clock-receiver roles. In a single-host receiving history with Link and Tempo Follower off, explicitly change the known host between two independently accepted tempos, retaining source traffic and Live tempo/transport observations. Keep the MTC manual-tempo/directional comparison separate. No guessed MIDI bytes, tick count, supported range, delay, tracking/convergence tolerance or transport-command sequence is an oracle.
references.assessment: context/partial prerequisite only; does not specify named Hardware Resync selector, button action or its three mode roles

references.quoted_scoped_predicate: With known destination connected and selected for Sync, inspect lower indicator while retaining independently observed transmitted clock traffic and receiver baseline; then disable this destination alone.

references.quoted_scoped_predicate: Retain two independently audible nonzero percussive patterns and usable sync; select the intended MIDI device and change accepted Sync Delay values while separately recording both outputs. Listening guidance is not a numerical comparator.

references.quoted_scoped_predicate: The MIDI settings distinguish Track for note/CC traffic, Sync for clock/timecode use and Remote for controller mapping/feedback. These roles do not establish sync protocol, arbitrary hardware support or mapping takeover behavior.
references.assessment: context/partial prerequisite only; does not specify named Hardware Resync selector, button action or its three mode roles

references.quoted_scoped_predicate: On available test input/output ports inspect Track/Sync/Remote separately and track their visible states. Do not send clock/resync to real gear or infer control-surface support.

references.quoted_scoped_predicate: F-MIDI: retain an unmatched note/CC positive track baseline; separately compare the same eligible message with a deliberate Remote mapping and Track/Remote combinations. references.quoted_scoped_predicate: An unlisted control surface can be set up for manual mapping through MIDI Ports. This workflow uses the routing owner's Remote input/output roles, rather than redefining Track/Sync/Remote or promising arbitrary hardware support.
